<div class="resource-page data-catalog-page">
  <section class="resource-hero" aria-labelledby="data-title">
  <div>
  <p class="eyebrow">Data catalogue</p>
  <h1 id="data-title">Course datasets</h1>
  <p>This page gathers the datasets used in STT-1100. It helps students find downloadable files, datasets provided by R packages and short profiles for local files.</p>
  <div class="resource-actions" aria-label="Quick links">
  <a class="home-action home-action--primary" href="#use-catalogue">Start</a>
  <a class="home-action" href="#catalogue-by-module">By module</a>
  <a class="home-action" href="#local-file-profiles">Local profiles</a>
  <a class="home-action" href="packages.html">R packages</a>
  </div>
  </div>
  <div class="resource-panel" aria-label="Catalogue landmarks">
  <div><span>CSV</span><p>Files to import and clean</p></div>
  <div><span>R</span><p>Datasets included in packages</p></div>
  <div><span>JSON</span><p>Nested data and lists</p></div>
  <div><span>XLS</span><p>Practice Excel sheets</p></div>
  </div>
  </section>

  <section class="resource-section" id="use-catalogue" aria-labelledby="data-use-title">
  <div class="resource-section__header">
  <p class="eyebrow">Working method</p>
  <h2 id="data-use-title">Use the catalogue</h2>
  <p>Each card gives a quick preview, a link to the local profile when the file is provided, or a link to the package when the data come from R. The catalogue does not replace the module instructions: it mainly helps you find the right dataset and understand its role.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="course-flow">
  <article class="flow-card">
  <span class="flow-number">1</span>
  <h3>Find the module</h3>
  <p>Start from the module connected to the exercise, adventure or challenge. The cards preserve this progression.</p>
  </article>
  <article class="flow-card">
  <span class="flow-number">2</span>
  <h3>Identify the type</h3>
  <p>A local file is downloaded; package data are loaded with R; a web page requires careful collection.</p>
  </article>
  <article class="flow-card">
  <span class="flow-number">3</span>
  <h3>Import from the right folder</h3>
  <p>In exercises, paths such as <code>data/file.csv</code> are relative to the module folder.</p>
  </article>
  <article class="flow-card">
  <span class="flow-number">4</span>
  <h3>Document the source</h3>
  <p>A reproducible report always says where the data come from and what they can, or cannot, support.</p>
  </article>
  </div>
  </section>

  <section class="resource-section" id="data-types" aria-labelledby="data-types-title">
  <div class="resource-section__header">
  <p class="eyebrow">Quick landmarks</p>
  <h2 id="data-types-title">Which type of data are you looking for?</h2>
  <p>The course datasets do not all serve the same purpose. Some are for practising basics, others for working with formats, joins, ethics or communication.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="reading-map">
  <article>
  <h3>Local files</h3>
  <p>CSV, JSON, Excel, RDS and HTML files provided with the modules. They are most useful for independent exercises.</p>
  </article>
  <article>
  <h3>Package datasets</h3>
  <p>Datasets accessible from R, useful for learning before managing file paths in detail.</p>
  </article>
  <article>
  <h3>Web data</h3>
  <p>External pages or repositories used to discuss collection, technical limits and terms of use.</p>
  </article>
  <article>
  <h3>Fictitious data</h3>
  <p>Simulated data used to practise without exposing personal information or reproducing a real system.</p>
  </article>
  </div>
  </section>

  <section class="resource-section" id="data-troubleshooting" aria-labelledby="data-troubleshooting-title">
  <div class="resource-section__header">
  <p class="eyebrow">Troubleshooting</p>
  <h2 id="data-troubleshooting-title">When importing does not work</h2>
  <p>Before changing code at random, check these four points. They solve most problems with course files.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="resource-hub-grid">
  <article>
  <h3>File path</h3>
  <p>Open the project or module folder before using a relative path such as <code>data/file.csv</code>.</p>
  </article>
  <article>
  <h3>Separator</h3>
  <p>A CSV can use a comma or a semicolon. Choose <code>read_csv()</code> or <code>read_delim()</code> according to the file.</p>
  </article>
  <article>
  <h3>Format</h3>
  <p>Excel, JSON, RDS and HTML are not read with the same function. The useful package is listed on the R packages page.</p>
  </article>
  <article>
  <h3>Interpretation</h3>
  <p>Fictitious data are for learning a method; they should not be described as evidence about the real world.</p>
  </article>
  </div>
  </section>
</div>
```

read_preview <- function(row, n = 50) {
  path <- project_file(row$path)
  extension <- tolower(tools::file_ext(path))

  if (extension == "csv") {
  return(readr::read_delim(
  file = path,
  delim = row$delimiter,
  n_max = n,
  show_col_types = FALSE,
  locale = readr::locale(encoding = "UTF-8")
  ))
  }

  if (extension == "xlsx") {
  return(readxl::read_excel(path, n_max = n))
  }

  if (extension == "json") {
  object <- jsonlite::read_json(path, simplifyVector = TRUE)
  if (is.data.frame(object)) {
  return(tibble::as_tibble(object))
  }
  if (is.list(object)) {
  return(tibble::tibble(
  element = names(object),
  value = purrr::map_chr(object, ~ paste(capture.output(str(.x, max.level = 1)), collapse = " "))
  ))
  }
  }

  if (extension == "rds") {
  object <- readRDS(path)
  if (is.data.frame(object)) {
  return(tibble::as_tibble(utils::head(object, n)))
  }
  return(tibble::tibble(type = class(object)[1], description = paste(dim(object), collapse = " x ")))
  }

  tibble::tibble(message = "No preview is available for this file type.")
}

profile_preview <- function(data) {
  tibble::tibble(
  variable = names(data),
  type = purrr::map_chr(data, ~ class(.x)[1]),
  missing_values_in_preview = purrr::map_int(data, ~ sum(is.na(.x))),
  distinct_values_in_preview = purrr::map_int(data, ~ dplyr::n_distinct(.x, na.rm = TRUE)),
  example = purrr::map_chr(data, function(x) {
  values <- x[!is.na(x)]
  if (length(values) == 0) return("NA")
  substr(as.character(values[[1]]), 1, 70)
  })
  )
}

display_preview <- function(data, max_rows = 12, max_cols = 12) {
  data <- utils::head(data, max_rows)
  if (ncol(data) > max_cols) {
  data <- data[, seq_len(max_cols), drop = FALSE]
  }
  data
}

dataset_facts <- function(row) {
  tibble::tibble(
  information = c("Module", "Observations", "Variables", "Course use", "Source", "License"),
  value = c(
  row$module,
  ifelse(is.na(row$rows), "Not determined automatically", format_integer_en(row$rows)),
  ifelse(is.na(row$cols), "Not determined automatically", format_integer_en(row$cols)),
  row$usage,
  row$source,
  row$license
  )
  )
}

card_href <- function(row) {
  if (identical(row$kind, "local")) return(paste0("#", row$id))
  if (identical(row$kind, "web") && !is.na(row$path)) return(row$path)
  if (!is.na(row$package_anchor)) return(paste0("packages.html#", row$package_anchor))
  "#"
}

render_dataset_card <- function(row) {
  href <- card_href(row)
  kind_label <- dplyr::case_when(
  row$kind == "local" ~ "Local file",
  row$kind == "package" ~ "R package",
  row$kind == "web" ~ "Web",
  row$kind == "text" ~ "Text",
  TRUE ~ "Dataset"
  )
  size_label <- ifelse(
  is.na(row$rows) & is.na(row$cols),
  "Structure to consult",
  paste0(
  ifelse(is.na(row$rows), "?", format_integer_en(row$rows)),
  " observations / ",
  ifelse(is.na(row$cols), "?", format_integer_en(row$cols)),
  " variables"
  )
  )
  action_label <- ifelse(row$kind == "local", "View profile", "View documentation")

  paste0(
  '<a id="dataset-card-', row$id, '" class="dataset-card" href="', href, '">',
  '<span class="resource-icon"><i class="bi ', row$icon, '"></i></span>',
  '<span>',
  '<span class="dataset-module">', html_text(row$module), '</span>',
  '<h2>', html_text(row$title), '</h2>',
  '<span class="resource-text">', html_text(row$description), '</span>',
  '<span class="dataset-meta"><span>', kind_label, '</span><span>', html_text(size_label), '</span></span>',
  '<span class="package-source">', action_label, '</span>',
  '</span>',
  '</a>'
  )
}

render_download_link <- function(row) {
  paste0(
  "<p class=\"dataset-download-wrap\"><a class=\"dataset-download\" href=\"",
  html_text(row$path),
  "\" download>Download ",
  html_text(basename(row$path)),
  "</a></p>"
  )
}
```

## Catalogue by module

```{r}
#| label: catalogue-by-module
#| results: asis

for (module_id in unique(dataset_catalog$module_id)) {
  module_rows <- dataset_catalog |> filter(.data$module_id ==.env$module_id)
  cat("### ", module_rows$module[[1]], " {#", module_id, "}\n\n", sep = "")
  cat("<div class=\"catalog-grid\">\n")
  purrr::walk(seq_len(nrow(module_rows)), ~ cat(render_dataset_card(module_rows[.x, ]), "\n"))
  cat("</div>\n\n")
}
```

## Local file profiles

Previews are limited to the first rows to keep the site light. Variable profiles are therefore quick diagnostics of the displayed preview, not exhaustive analyses of each full file.

```{r}
#| label: local-file-profiles
#| results: asis

local_rows <- dataset_catalog |> filter(.data$kind == "local")

for (index in seq_len(nrow(local_rows))) {
  row <- local_rows[index, ]
  cat("### ", row$title, " {#", row$id, "}\n\n", sep = "")
  cat(row$description, "\n\n")
  cat(render_download_link(row), "\n\n")

  print(knitr::kable(dataset_facts(row), col.names = c("Information", "Value")))
  cat("\n\n")

  preview <- tryCatch(read_preview(row, n = 50), error = function(error) {
  tibble::tibble(message = paste("Preview unavailable:", conditionMessage(error)))
  })

  cat("#### Preview\n\n")
  cat("Preview limited to 12 rows and 12 columns to keep the page light.\n\n")
  print(DT::datatable(display_preview(preview), rownames = FALSE, class = "compact stripe hover", options = list(pageLength = 6, scrollX = TRUE, dom = "tip")))
  cat("\n\n")

  cat("#### Preview variables\n\n")
  print(knitr::kable(profile_preview(preview)))
  cat("\n\n")
}
```
